section.title: Introduction
section.p: DitherExtend chooses colours for a screen mode, and where a mode has too few colours to show the one requested, builds a pattern of the colours that it does have so that the result looks like the colour asked for. It provides ordered and error-diffusion colour patterns for the 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 bits per pixel modes, halftone screens built from a spot function, and the blending routine used to antialias graphics against an existing background.

It extends the colour selection SWIs of ColourTrans. Callers which already use ColourTrans to pick colours receive dithered colours without change, while programs which want to control the dither or obtain the patterns themselves use the family directly. Displaying the patterns, drawing with them and the colour management of source images belong to the clients and to ColourTrans.

section.title: Overview
section.p: The module provides the SWIs of the group (SWI offsets &hex;00 to &hex;0D) with the same names and in the same order, so that a call to has the same shape as a call to . The results differ in that the module may build a pattern in place of a single solid colour. The remaining SWIs are extensions which give direct access to the patterns, the palette, the halftone screen and the antialiasing blenders.

Dithering is switched on and off by a hidden SWI. While it is switched on, calls to the ColourTrans-compatible SWIs are passed to so that every client of the colour system is dithered. A client which wants the module's own result for a single call suspends the pass-through first.
The behaviour of dithering is controlled by the command and by .

definition-table.definition: A colour specified as a 32 bit word, &hex;BBGGRR00, with blue in the top byte, then green, then red. The low byte is zero.

The value written into screen memory for a pixel (or the palette index in a mode with a palette). In 16 bits per pixel modes it is a 15 bit colour; in 32 bits per pixel modes it is the top 24 bits of the colour word.

The form of a colour number used with GCOL and the VDU drivers. It differs from the colour number only in 256 colour modes, where the tint bits are moved: bits 4 to 6 of the colour number are held in bits 3 to 5, and the tint is held in bit 6.
The screen depth, as the logarithm to base 2 of the number of bits per pixel: 0 (1 bit), 1 (2 bits), 2 (4 bits), 3 (8 bits), 4 (16 bits) and 5 (32 bits).
A mode number or a pointer to a mode selector, or -1 for the current mode.
A pointer to a block of palette words, 0 for the default palette of the mode's depth, or -1 for the current palette. The block holds 2, 4, 16 or 256 colour words according to the depth.

subsection.title: Choosing colours
subsection.p: The colour number SWIs find the palette entry nearest to the colour requested. The nearest entry is chosen differently according to the depth, and in 256 colour modes according to the kind of palette. A 256 colour palette is classified as the default palette, a grey ramp, a 6x6x6 colour cube, or a custom palette. The classification is made again whenever the palette changes, so that the fastest search suitable for the palette is used.
In 16 bits per pixel modes the colour is reduced to 15 bits. In 32 bits per pixel modes the colour number is the colour word shifted right by 8 bits, and no search is made.

The Opp SWIs return the palette entry which is farthest from the colour requested, rather than the nearest, for use where the contrast with a colour is needed. In 16 and 32 bits per pixel modes they return the colour word unchanged.

subsection.title: Dither flags
subsection.p:
The module keeps a flags word, which is read with and updated with and .
Blend two palette colours by error diffusion Blend three palette colours by error diffusion. Takes precedence over bit 0 Build a pattern from the luminance of the colour, using the palette colours Use ordered patterns in the 4 and 8 bits per pixel modes Reserved Dithering disabled: solid colours only (set by *Dither 1) Greyscale dither (set by *Dither 2) Alternative four colour dither (set by *Dither 4) Reserved

Bits 0 to 3 are the control bits and are changed by . Bits 16 to 18 are the option, and are changed only by . At a depth of 8 bits per pixel with a grey ramp palette, and in 16 bits per pixel modes with no flags set, a solid colour is always used.

subsection.title: Dither state and ColourV
subsection.p: The module is disabled when it is initialised. The hidden SWIs and change the state, and reads it. Enabling or disabling dithering also invalidates the palette information held by the module.

While the module is enabled, a call to any of the SWIs at offsets &hex;00 to &hex;0D is not handled directly. Instead the registers are passed to (vector &hex;22) with R8 holding the SWI offset and R9 holding the vector number, and the registers it returns are returned to the caller. makes the very next such call be handled by the module itself, after which the pass-through resumes. The other SWIs are never passed on.

subsection.title: Palettes and caches
subsection.p: The palette in use is read from the hardware when it is needed, and its classification is remembered until it is invalidated by , a change of mode or a change of palette. For modes of up to 8 bits per pixel the palette is held by the module and may be read with .

Memory for the larger tables is allocated from the module area when first needed: a 4096 byte blend table at 4 bits per pixel, a &hex;9000 byte colour search cache for custom palettes at 8 bits per pixel, and a &hex;20000 byte block returned by . They are all freed when the palette changes, when the mode changes, on reset and when the module is finalised.

subsection.title: Colour patterns
subsection.p: A colour pattern is the arrangement of palette colours which, viewed from a distance, represents a colour that the mode cannot display directly. , and return patterns as 32 byte buffers. A buffer holds eight words, alternating between the pixels of an even scan line and the pixels of an odd scan line, and so describes a pattern 32 bits wide and 8 lines tall in the format of the current depth. The pattern is rotated by the halftone origin so that adjacent areas of the same colour line up.

and build the same pattern, but write it into the pattern area of the VDU drivers so that it becomes the current graphics colour. The address of the pattern area is read from VDU variable &hex;AB when the module starts. The pattern area has room for two patterns of 16 words each; the foreground pattern is the first, and the background pattern follows it. Bit 7 of R3 selects the background pattern. Where a solid colour is sufficient, the GCOL value is returned in R0 as for .

subsection.title: Halftone screens
subsection.p:
A halftone screen replaces the pattern selection with a threshold screen, so that the grey level of a colour is compared with the thresholds to choose between two colours. The screen is described by eight words, set with and read back with :
pointer to the thresholds, one byte for each position, or 0 if no screen is set width of the screen in pixels height of the screen in pixels shift between successive rows colour number used where the threshold is not exceeded colour number used where the threshold is exceeded reserved for the module, set to 0 reserved for the module, set to 0

builds a screen from a spot function, and sets these values itself. converts the screen for one threshold into a bitmap that can be used directly as a pattern. A change of mode cancels the halftone screen.
The halftone origin, set with , fixes where the screen starts, so that screens drawn at different times join up.

subsection.title: Antialiasing
subsection.p:
does not blend pixels itself. It returns a pointer to the module's workspace and a pointer to a blending routine suitable for the current depth. The caller invokes the routine directly. The routine is chosen from the depth, and for 8 bits per pixel modes from the palette type (default, grey ramp, colour cube or custom). The routines are entered with:
IP = the workspace pointer returned in R0
R1 = pointer to the mask, one weight byte for each pixel
R2 = pointer to the source pixels
R3 = pointer to the destination pixels, which are updated
R4 = number of pixels

A weight of 0 leaves the destination pixel unchanged, a weight of 16 copies the source pixel, and values between give a proportional mixture of the source and destination colours. The routine returns by loading R0 to IP and PC from the stack, so the caller must have stacked R0 to IP and the address to return to, in that order, before entering it. At 1 and 2 bits per pixel the count is rounded up in groups of 4 pixels. The routines do not depend on the caller's static base register and may be used from any code.

use.p: The module frees the memory it holds for its caches. Its state is otherwise left as it was.
The module reads the new screen depth and eigenvalue factors, invalidates the palette classification, frees its caches, cancels any halftone screen and resets the halftone origin to 0,0.
The module treats a palette change as it does a change of mode, and so discards its knowledge of the palette, its caches and the halftone screen.

section.title: SWI calls
section.p: The SWI chunk is &hex;44580 and the SWI names are prefixed with DitherExtend_. Offsets &hex;00 to &hex;0D are the ColourTrans-compatible SWIs. Any SWI offset from &hex;20 to &hex;3B, or above &hex;3F, returns the error . Unless an error is returned, registers not listed as output are preserved.

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_SelectTable
swi-definition.description: Builds a table converting the colours of one mode to colour numbers in another

entry.register-use: source palette (a palette argument), or 0 for the default
destination palette (a palette argument), or 0 for the default
pointer to the buffer for the table

use.p: For each colour in the source palette, one entry is written to the buffer with the colour number of the nearest colour in the destination mode. The entries are one byte for each colour at 1, 2, 4 and 8 bits per pixel, two bytes at 16 bits per pixel and four bytes at 32 bits per pixel. The source mode must have no more than 8 bits per pixel.
It has the same interface as , and is the target of that call while dithering is enabled.
Errors are returned if either mode is invalid ().

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_SelectGCOLTable
swi-definition.description: Builds a table converting the colours of one mode to GCOL values in another

entry.register-use: pointer to the buffer for the table

use.p: This is as , except that when the destination mode has 256 colours the entries are converted to GCOL values.

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_ReturnGCOL
swi-definition.description: Returns the GCOL value for a colour in the current mode

use.p: Returns the colour number of the nearest colour in the current mode, converted to a GCOL value in 256 colour modes. In other modes the colour number is returned.

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_SetGCOL
swi-definition.description: Sets the graphics colour, building a dither pattern if required

entry.register-use:
flags:
set the foreground pattern set the background pattern ignored ignored
mask row, of which only bits 0 to 2 are used

exit.register-use: GCOL value of the nearest solid colour

use.p: Builds the pattern for the colour in the pattern area of the VDU drivers, as described under . The mask row selects one of 8 masks which are applied to the pattern rows. Where a halftone screen has been set, the grey level of the colour is retained for use by instead of a pattern being built.

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_ReturnColourNumber
swi-definition.description: Returns the colour number for a colour in the current mode

use.p: Returns the colour number of the palette entry nearest to the colour, without conversion to a GCOL value.

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_ReturnGCOLForMode
swi-definition.description: Returns the GCOL value for a colour in a given mode

use.p: As but for the mode and palette given. Returns the error if the mode is not valid.

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_ReturnColourNumberForMode
swi-definition.description: Returns the colour number for a colour in a given mode

use.p: As but for the mode and palette given. Returns the error if the mode is not valid.

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_ReturnOppGCOL
swi-definition.description: Returns the GCOL value of the palette colour farthest from a colour

use.p: Returns the GCOL value of the palette entry in the current mode which is farthest from the colour.

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_SetOppGCOL
swi-definition.description: Sets the graphics colour to the colour farthest from a colour

exit.register-use: GCOL value of the colour used

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_ReturnOppColourNumber
swi-definition.description: Returns the colour number of the palette colour farthest from a colour

use.p: Returns the colour number of the palette entry in the current mode which is farthest from the colour.

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_ReturnOppGCOLForMode
swi-definition.description: Returns the GCOL value of the palette colour farthest from a colour in a given mode

use.p: As but for the mode and palette given. Returns the error if the mode is not valid.

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_ReturnOppColourNumberForMode
swi-definition.description: Returns the colour number of the palette colour farthest from a colour in a given mode

use.p: As but for the mode and palette given. Returns the error if the mode is not valid.

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_GCOLToColourNumber
swi-definition.description: Converts a GCOL value to a colour number

use.p: Converts a GCOL value for a 256 colour mode to the colour number. It does not depend on the current mode.

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_ColourNumberToGCOL
swi-definition.description: Converts a colour number to a GCOL value

use.p: Converts a colour number for a 256 colour mode to the GCOL value. It does not depend on the current mode.

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_Info
swi-definition.description: Reads the dither flags

use.p: Returns the dither flags, as described under .

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_Control
swi-definition.description: Changes the dither control bits

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_ReturnColourPattern
swi-definition.description: Returns the colour pattern for a colour in the current mode

use.p: Writes the pattern which would be set for the colour by into the buffer, in the format described under .

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_ReturnColourPatternTable
swi-definition.description: Returns the patterns for a ramp of colours

entry.register-use: pointer to a buffer of 8192 bytes

use.p: Writes 256 patterns into the buffer, each of 32 bytes. The colours are evenly spaced from the first colour to the last colour, and the pattern for each is as returned by .

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_InvalidatePalette
swi-definition.description: Discards the module's knowledge of the palette

use.p: Reads the palette again and classifies it, and frees the caches. This is called by clients which have changed the hardware palette without the module being told through . In 16 and 32 bits per pixel modes no palette is read.

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_Antialias
swi-definition.description: Returns the antialiasing blend routine for the current mode

use.p: Chooses a blending routine according to the depth of the current mode, as described under , and allocates the tables it needs. The pointers remain valid until the next mode or palette change. Returns the error if the depth cannot be handled.

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_ReadPalette
swi-definition.description: Reads the palette of a mode

use.p: Copies the palette words into the buffer: 2, 4, 16 or 256 words according to the depth. The mode must have no more than 8 bits per pixel.

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_ReturnColourPatternArray
swi-definition.description: Returns the block of memory used for the pattern array

exit.register-use: pointer to the block of &hex;20000 bytes

use.p: Returns the module's array of patterns. The block is allocated the first time it is requested and remains until the caches are freed.

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_SetHalftone
swi-definition.description: Sets the halftone screen

use.p: Stores the eight words. If R0 is non-zero, a halftone screen is in use for subsequent calls. R0 of 0 removes the screen. The thresholds are not copied, and must remain valid for as long as the screen is in use.

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_ReturnHalftone
swi-definition.description: Reads the halftone screen

exit.register-use: halftone description, or R0 = 0 if no screen is set

use.p: Returns the eight words set by or . If there is no screen then only R0 is written, and it is 0.

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_SetHalftoneOrigin
swi-definition.description: Sets the origin of the halftone screen

use.p: Sets the point on the screen from which the halftone screen and the colour patterns are aligned. The coordinates are relative to the current graphics origin. The x coordinate is stored as a bit position in the screen row and the y coordinate as a line counted from the top of the screen. Both are reset to 0 by a change of mode.

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_ReturnHalftoneOrigin
swi-definition.description: Reads the origin of the halftone screen

exit.register-use: x origin, as a bit position in the screen row
y origin, as a line counted from the top of the screen

use.p: Returns the values calculated by .

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_SelectHalftoneTable
swi-definition.description: Builds a table of grey levels for the colours of a mode

use.p: Writes one byte for each colour in the palette, giving its grey level from 0 to 255. The mode must have no more than 8 bits per pixel. Returns the error if the mode is not valid.

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_ReturnHalftoneIntensity
swi-definition.description: Returns the grey level of a colour

use.p: Returns the luminance of the colour, weighted for the sensitivity of the eye to each of the primaries.

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_ReturnHalftoneTable
swi-definition.description: Returns the grey levels of a ramp of colours

entry.register-use: pointer to a buffer of 256 bytes

use.p: Writes 256 bytes giving the grey level of the colours spaced evenly from the first colour to the last.

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_SetScreen
swi-definition.description: Builds a halftone screen from a spot function

entry.register-use:
spot function:
round dot: the spot grows from the centre of the cell, and the background grows from its edges inverse of function -3 elliptical: the sum of the squares of the distance from the centre of the cell line: the distance on the vertical axis alone cross: the smaller of the distances on the two axes round dot repeated at twice the frequency pointer to a user routine
screen angle, in degrees as a 16.16 fixed point number
x size of the screen cell
y size of the screen cell
cell argument which scales the screen lattice
colour number used where the threshold is not exceeded
colour number used where the threshold is exceeded

use.p: Builds the thresholds for a halftone screen of the angle and cell size requested, ranking the positions of the cell by the value of the spot function so that the screen is evenly graded from 0 to 255. The module owns the thresholds, and sets the halftone screen to use them, as if had been called. A cell of up to 1024 positions is supported.

A user routine is called with R0 = x and R1 = y, signed fixed point numbers where 1.0 is &hex;10000, and returns the value in R2 as a signed fixed point number where 1.0 is &hex;1000000. Registers other than R0 to R2 must be preserved.
Returns the error if the cell is too large, or is degenerate for the angle.

p.fixme: The units of R2 to R4 are not established from the source.

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_CacheScreen
swi-definition.description: Converts the halftone screen at one threshold to a bitmap

exit.register-use: pointer to the bitmap, or 0 if the screen cannot be cached
width in bits of one row of the bitmap

use.p: Compares each threshold with the key and packs the result into a bitmap in the format of the current depth, using the two colours of the halftone screen. A row narrower than a word is repeated to fill the word. The bitmap is held by the module, and the last result is returned again if the same key is given twice. No bitmap is returned if no screen is set, if the depth is more than 8 bits per pixel, or if the bitmap would be larger than 64 words.

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_SelectColourPatternTable
swi-definition.description: Builds a table of patterns for the colours of a mode

use.p: Writes a 32 byte pattern for each colour of the palette, in the format used by . The buffer must be 32 bytes for each palette entry.

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_ReadDitherState
swi-definition.description: Reads whether dithering is enabled

exit.register-use:
state:
Calls are passed to ColourV The next call is handled by the module Reserved

use.p: This SWI has no name in the module's SWI table, and is called by number. It can be called while dithering is in any state.

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_SuspendDither
swi-definition.description: Handles the next call in the module instead of passing it to ColourV

use.p: If dithering is enabled, the next call to a SWI at offsets &hex;00 to &hex;0D is handled by the module itself, and the state then returns to that of passing calls to . This allows a handler of to ask for the module's own result. It has no effect if dithering is disabled. This SWI has no name in the module's SWI table, and is called by number.

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_EnableDither
swi-definition.description: Enables dithering

use.p: Enables dithering, so that calls to the ColourTrans-compatible SWIs are passed to . The palette information is invalidated. This SWI has no name in the module's SWI table, and is called by number.

swi-definition.name: DitherExtend_DisableDither
swi-definition.description: Disables dithering

use.p: Disables dithering, so that all of the SWIs are handled by the module. The palette information is invalidated. This SWI has no name in the module's SWI table, and is called by number.

parameter.name: dither option
parameter.p:
The option, from 0 to 255, of which only the low three bits are used:
Use the default dither Disable dithering Use a greyscale dither Use the alternative four colour dither

use.p: Sets the option in bits 16 to 18 of the dither flags. The control bits are not changed. If no option is given, the default dither is used.

error-definition.name: DitherNoColourTrans
error-definition.description: ColourTrans needs to be installed before DitherExtend

use.p: Returned when the module is initialised and ColourTrans is not present.
Returned when a mode argument does not describe a screen mode, or describes a mode whose depth the SWI does not support.
Returned by when the cell for the angle and size requested has more positions than the module can hold, or has none.
Returned when the SWI offset is not one of the SWIs provided by the module.

subsection.title: Reading a colour pattern
subsection.p: This reads the pattern used for mid-grey in the current mode and then reads its grey level.

p.extended-example:
Pattern for a colour
DIM pattern% 32
SYS "DitherExtend_ReturnColourPattern", &80808000, 0, pattern%
SYS "DitherExtend_ReturnHalftoneIntensity", &80808000 TO grey%
PRINT "Grey level ";grey%

subsection.title: Selecting a dither option
subsection.p: This selects the greyscale dither from a program, and sets bit 1 of the control bits (three colour error diffusion), leaving the other control bits as they were.

p.extended-example:
Select the dither
OSCLI "Dither 2"
SYS "DitherExtend_Control", 2, NOT 2 TO flags%
PRINT "Flags &";~flags%

subsection.title: Blending with the antialias routine
subsection.p: This obtains the blender and calls it to mix a row of source pixels into the destination. The code is entered with the mask, source, destination and pixel count in R5 to R8.

p.extended-example:
Antialias a row of pixels
SWI "DitherExtend_Antialias"
MOVVS pc, lr ; Bad mode, or no room
MOV r9, r1 ; the blend routine
MOV ip, r0 ; IP = workspace
ADR lr, done
STMFD sp!, {r0-ip, lr} ; the routine pops these and returns to done
MOV r1, r5 ; mask
MOV r2, r6 ; source
MOV r3, r7 ; destination
MOV r4, r8 ; pixel count
MOV pc, r9
done

section.title: Compatibility
section.p: The SWIs at offsets &hex;00 to &hex;0D have the interface of the ColourTrans SWIs of the same names, and may be used in their place. The module requires ColourTrans to be loaded before it is started.
